item.title: Tech Volatility Hits Highest Since Dot-Com Bust Next to S&P 500
item.description: The higher the rally in technology high-flyers, the louder the anxiety around a new wave of turbulence in the group.

item.title: Tech Weakness Resumes After Samsung Misses Lofty AI Expectations
item.description: US stock futures pointed to renewed weakness in technology shares after Samsung Electronics Co.’s earnings failed to satisfy investors, renewing pressure on chipmakers across global markets.

item.title: Geothermal Startup Raises $144 Million to Drill Superhot Rocks
item.description: Geothermal startup Quaise Energy raised $144 million to develop technology for drilling superhot rocks.

item.title: Fincantieri Says Hybrid Warfare Is Growing Threat to Europe Seas
item.description: Hybrid warfare presents an emerging threat to Europe’s underwater cable and energy links, the chief executive officer of Italian shipbuilder Fincantieri SpA said.

item.title: Chinese AI Startup DeepSeek Developing Own AI Chip, Report Says
item.description: China’s DeepSeek is developing its own chip to help power artificial intelligence systems, Reuters reported, citing unnamed sources.

item.title: VC Money Doubles In Defense Tech as the Next Big Bet
item.description: Startups focused on aerospace and the military are no longer off limits for Silicon Valley

item.title: Reflections From Pierre Yared, a Departing Member of ‘Brainiac’ Trump Team
item.description: Trump policies may shock, but they offer US allies an example of how to strengthen themselves, Yared says

item.title: Forced-Labor Hearings in US Kick Off Fresh Tariff Debate
item.description: Three days of panels are scheduled, in the process to rebuild Trump’s tariff agenda

item.title: Iraq Boosts Oil Output at Three Southern Fields to Full Capacity
item.description: Iraq has raised production from three key projects in the country’s oil heartland to full capacity as tankers have started arriving to export cargoes, a person familiar with the operations said.

item.title: Mag 7 Loses Market Swagger as AI Trade Spreads Beyond Behemoths
item.description: For years, the Magnificent Seven tech giants commanded investors’ attention, dominating the S&P 500 Index and determining which way the overall stock market was headed. Those days are over.

item.title: Britain Needs £100 Billion a Year to Stabilize Public Debt, Watchdog Says
item.description: Andy Burnham faces a £100 billion ($134 billion) challenge if he wants to put Britain’s public finances on a sustainable path, the government’s fiscal watchdog warned.

item.title: SAP’s Senior Reshuffle Follows AI-Induced Stock Rout
item.description: The SaaSpocalypse might as well have been called the SAPocalypse.

item.title: Ex-Tesla Scientist Unveils Plans For European Humanoid Robot
item.description: A former Tesla Inc. scientist who worked on Elon Musk’s Optimus robot unveiled plans to produce a lightweight humanoid robot for manufacturing plants, logistics warehouses and homes.

item.title: Wall Street Buys Into Musk’s SpaceX Vision
item.description: SpaceX is joining the Nasdaq 100 Index and analysts at big global brokers are recommending investors buy shares.

item.title: France Cuts 2026 GDP Forecast Due to Budget Delay, Iran Conflict
item.description: The French government is lowering its growth forecast for the year to 0.7% after a delayed budget and the Middle East conflict held back output, Finance Minister Roland Lescure told Le Parisien newspaper.

item.title: AI Productivity Gains Are Years Away, Deutsche Bank’s Reid Says
item.description: Artificial intelligence is likely to enhance productivity signficantly but any such impact on economies may still be years away, Deutsche Bank analyst Jim Reid said.

item.title: A Once-Great Copper Miner Faces a Reckoning Just as AI Power Demand Soars
item.description: Chile’s Codelco, facing scrutiny for a fatal accident and inflated production figures, is struggling under $25 billion of debt.

item.title: Chile revisa el futuro de Codelco en medio del boom mundial de la demanda de cobre
item.description: A medida que se dispara la demanda mundial de cobre, una de las mayores empresas mineras del mundo se encuentra en una situación precaria.

item.title: BOE Lifts Veil on Private Financing of 520 British Companies
item.description: Alternative asset managers have given the Bank of England detailed information on their investments in 520 UK corporates with revenue of more than £230 billion ($308 billion), as part of the watchdog’s probe into potential economic fallout from a private markets crash.

item.title: BOE Proposes Easing Some Capital Rules Despite Mounting Risks
item.description: The Bank of England has proposed easing a handful of capital rules, even as officials fret about deepening threats from AI, a fraught geopolitical outlook and rapidly increasing leverage.

item.title: Goldman Says Earnings to Drive More Gains in Asset-Heavy Stocks
item.description: Capital-intensive companies are likely to report solid earnings this season, further outperforming peers that are more reliant on human or digital assets, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc. strategists.

item.title: LNG Tanker Attack Threatens Qatar’s Efforts to Revive Hormuz Exports
item.description: A projectile hit the Al Rekayyat gas carrier on Tuesday, with the repercussions reverberating through the global gas market.

item.title: Renewables Hit Record Share of India Power Mix as Coal Flatlines
item.description: The share of renewable energy in India’s electricity mix rose to a record high this summer, highlighting the increasing importance of solar and wind in the world’s third-largest emitter.

item.title: Extreme SK Hynix Stock Swings Add Wild Card to $28 Billion Deal
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s New York listing, currently on track to be the largest ever by a foreign company in the US, is facing an unusual source of uncertainty for a major offering: the wildest swings seen in global chip stocks in years.

item.title: De Beers Makes Deep Diamond Price Cuts for Shrinking Buyers Club
item.description: De Beers has made some of the deepest ever cuts to its official diamond prices, potentially signaling an end to its years-long campaign to hold them well above the market rate.

item.title: ECB Asks Banks for Plans to Address AI Cybersecurity Threats
item.description: Europe’s banking regulator asked banks to come up with plans to address the growing threat from frontier artificial intelligence models such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude Mythos to cybersecurity.

item.title: China Regulator Is Keeping a Close Eye on Susquehanna Case
item.description: China’s securities watchdog said it is paying close attention to a legal case brought by Susquehanna International Group against alleged insider traders, after the US market maker said regulatory officials may have been involved in the trades.

item.title: Uzbekistan’s AKFA Picks Citi, JPM to Sound Out Bond Investors
item.description: AKFA Aluminium Group, one of Uzbekistan’s largest private companies, is set to meet international investors next week as it explores issuing its first ever bond.

item.title: China’s PBOC Buys Most Gold Since 2023 as Bullion Swings
item.description: China’s central bank bought more gold in June, extending the longest buying streak since at least 2015 and underscoring a commitment to diversifying its reserves despite volatility in bullion prices.

item.title: Italy Revives Dollar Bond Sales for First Time Since Pandemic
item.description: Italy is returning to the US dollar bond market for the first time since the pandemic, broadening its pool of foreign investors after the country’s improving finances won credit-rating upgrades.
